title: Mechanisms of Projective Composition of Diffusion Models

claude.title: Mechanisms of Projective Composition of Diffusion Models
claude.idea: Defines projective composition and proves when a linear combination of scores achieves it, using a factorized-conditionals independence condition.
claude.models: Conditional diffusion models on CLEVR; SDXL fine-tuned on one dog for an illustration
claude.headline_result: not stated
claude.evidence_quote: Then, we investigate: (1) when linear score combinations provably achieve projective composition, (2) whether reverse-diffusion sampling can generate the desired composition, and (3) the conditions under which composition fails.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: Mechanisms of Projective Composition of Diffusion Models
astra.idea: Defines composition by preserved projected marginals and proves score composition and reverse diffusion valid under factorized conditionals, while general feature-space composition need not be sampleable by reverse diffusion.
astra.models: Conditional diffusion scores with a background score; CLEVR diffusion models. Setup: the theory permits sources that are not conditionals of a shared joint distribution; the successful construction requires compatible factors and a background distribution.
astra.datasets: CLEVR object-location and object-color composition experiments.
astra.headline_result: not stated
astra.evidence_quote: We begin by precisely defining one possible desired result of composition, which we call projective composition.

title: Compositional Visual Generation with Composable Diffusion Models

claude.title: Compositional Visual Generation with Composable Diffusion Models
claude.idea: Treats each diffusion model as an energy function and adds their noise predictions at sampling time so one image satisfies several concepts.
claude.models: Composed diffusion models trained on CLEVR and FFHQ; pre-trained GLIDE and Stable Diffusion for text
claude.datasets: CLEVR, Relational CLEVR, FFHQ, text prompts
claude.headline_result: CLEVR with 3 components at 128x128: binary classification accuracy 31.36% and FID 10.51, against 7.34% and 58.33 for the EBM baseline
claude.evidence_quote: An image is generated by composing a set of diffusion models, with each of them modeling a certain component of the image.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: Compositional Visual Generation with Composable Diffusion Models
astra.idea: Adds or subtracts conditional diffusion scores to express concept conjunction and negation, but reports limited success when the models were trained on different datasets.
astra.models: Self-composed conditional diffusion models; pretrained text-guided diffusion models including GLIDE; Section 7 notes that successful components are instances of the same model. Setup: composition uses separate conditions; however, the training images can contain multiple objects, so the experiments do not establish the strict disjoint-data setup.
astra.datasets: CLEVR; Relational CLEVR; FFHQ; text-description composition examples.
astra.headline_result: Three-component CLEVR accuracy 31.36% and FID 10.51.
astra.evidence_quote: An image is generated by composing a set of diffusion models, with each of them modeling a certain component of the image.

title: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle: Compositional Generation with Energy-Based Diffusion Models and MCMC

claude.title: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle: Compositional Generation with Energy-Based Diffusion Models and MCMC
claude.idea: Blames failed composition on the reverse sampler and replaces it with annealed MCMC samplers, including Metropolis-corrected ones on an energy parameterization.
claude.models: Score-based and energy-based diffusion models; Imagen 64x64 base model for image tapestries
claude.datasets: 2D distributions, CLEVR cube positions, ImageNet 128x128 classifier guidance, composed text prompts
claude.headline_result: CLEVR with 5 cube positions: 72.7% of samples place every object correctly with the energy model and HMC, against 57.4% for reverse sampling of the score model
claude.evidence_quote: We conclude that the sampler (not the model) is responsible for this failure and propose new samplers, inspired by MCMC, which enable successful compositional generation.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle: Compositional Generation with Energy-Based Diffusion Models and MCMC
astra.idea: Replaces naive reverse sampling of composed scores with annealed MCMC, with energy parameterization enabling Metropolis-corrected samplers.
astra.models: Score-parameterized and energy-parameterized diffusion models; ULA, U-HMC, MALA and HMC; self-composed text-to-image models. Setup: combines individual condition scores; CLEVR training still contains multi-object images and is not the strict disjoint single-concept setup.
astra.datasets: Synthetic densities; CLEVR; ImageNet; composed text prompts and image tapestries.
astra.headline_result: Five-position CLEVR accuracy 72.7 for energy-parameterized HMC versus 57.4 for score-parameterized reverse sampling.
astra.evidence_quote: We conclude that the sampler (not the model) is responsible for this failure and propose new samplers, inspired by MCMC, which enable successful compositional generation.

title: Catastrophic Compositional Generation: Why Vanilla Diffusion Models Fail to Extrapolate

claude.title: Catastrophic Compositional Generation: Why Vanilla Diffusion Models Fail to Extrapolate
claude.idea: Argues that when the composed target lies outside the training distributions, score estimation error dominates and inference-time correction such as Feynman-Kac cannot fix it.
claude.models: Conditional diffusion models and separately trained diffusion models
claude.datasets: 2D Gaussians, Gaussian mixtures, semi-synthetic room images
claude.headline_result: Out-of-distribution Gaussian mixture with 256 particles: sliced Wasserstein-2 distance to the target 1.4670 with analytic scores, against 2.6706 with scores learned from 10,000 samples
claude.evidence_quote: In particular, while recent methods such as Feynman-Kac correction reduce inference-time approximation error, our results show that score estimation error has a more catastrophic effect on performance when the target distribution is out-of-distribution with respect to the sources, highlighting the need for a different approach to this task.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: Catastrophic Compositional Generation: Why Vanilla Diffusion Models Fail to Extrapolate
astra.idea: Separates sampler approximation error from out-of-distribution score error and shows that Feynman-Kac correction can amplify the latter, including for separately trained experts.
astra.models: Conditional denoising diffusion models and separately trained single-condition experts; analytic-score controls; FKC. Setup: explicitly tests target combinations absent from source training support, alongside in-distribution controls.
astra.datasets: Synthetic Gaussians and Gaussian mixtures; semi-synthetic rooms containing couches, paintings, or coffee tables.
astra.headline_result: In the non-factorized OOD Gaussian setting with N=10000, SW2 worsens from 0.8518 at K=1 to 2.8322 at K=256; analytic-score SW2 improves from 0.6375 to 0.0820.
astra.evidence_quote: Moreover, in these cases, we find that FKC reinforces these errors, further degenerating sample quality.

title: Feynman-Kac Correctors in Diffusion: Annealing, Guidance, and Product of Experts

claude.title: Feynman-Kac Correctors in Diffusion: Annealing, Guidance, and Product of Experts
claude.idea: Derives importance weights from the Feynman-Kac formula and resamples particles so sampling follows annealed, geometric-mean or product targets built from pretrained score models.
claude.models: EDM2-XS on ImageNet-512 for images; pretrained molecule models
claude.headline_result: EDM2 at noise level 40 and 32 steps over 10,000 images: CLIP 29.00 and ImageReward 0.04 with FKC, against 28.75 and -0.24 with CFG alone (the right half of the same table prints 29.14 and 0.05 for this setting)
claude.evidence_quote: In this work, we provide an efficient and principled method for sampling from a sequence of annealed, geometric-averaged, or product distributions derived from pretrained score-based models.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: Feynman-Kac Correctors in Diffusion: Annealing, Guidance, and Product of Experts
astra.idea: Uses Feynman-Kac particle weights and sequential Monte Carlo resampling to track annealed or composed distributions more faithfully.
astra.models: Pretrained score models; EDM2-XS for image guidance; DEM for temperature annealing; pretrained molecular models. Setup: operates on pretrained scores without target joint training data or a joint prompt; accuracy still depends on those scores.
astra.datasets: ImageNet-512; synthetic multimodal distributions; Lennard-Jones systems; multi-objective molecule generation.
astra.headline_result: EDM2+FKC achieves CLIP 29.14 and ImageReward 0.05 at churn 40 and 32 steps, compared with 28.75 and -0.24 without FKC.
astra.evidence_quote: To simulate these PDEs, we propose Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) resampling algorithms that leverage inference-time scaling to improve sampling quality.

title: The Superposition of Diffusion Models Using the Itô Density Estimator

claude.title: The Superposition of Diffusion Models Using the Itô Density Estimator
claude.idea: Combines pretrained diffusion models during sampling with weights from a new Itô density estimator, giving OR and AND style superpositions.
claude.models: Stable Diffusion v1-4; CIFAR-10 models; Proteus and FrameDiff; molecule models
claude.datasets: CIFAR-10 split into two disjoint partitions, 20 Stable Diffusion concept pairs, proteins, molecules
claude.headline_result: Stable Diffusion concept pairs, 20 images for each of 20 pairs: minimum TIFA 39.92 for SuperDiff AND, against 32.48 for averaged scores and 27.58 for joint prompting
claude.evidence_quote: We demonstrate that SuperDiff is scalable to large pre-trained diffusion models as superposition is performed solely through composition during inference, and also enjoys painless implementation as it combines different pre-trained vector fields through an automated re-weighting scheme.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: The Superposition of Diffusion Models Using the Itô Density Estimator
astra.idea: SuperDiff dynamically reweights pretrained vector fields using estimated densities to implement OR and equal-likelihood AND composition, with image AND experiments targeting concept blending.
astra.models: Separate diffusion models; Stable Diffusion v1-4; FrameDiff and Proteus; LDMol. Setup: composes pretrained models or separate prompts without retraining; joint prompts are comparison baselines.
astra.datasets: CIFAR-10; concept-pair image interpolation prompts; protein and multi-property molecule generation.
astra.headline_result: Image concept interpolation minimum TIFA 39.92 versus 32.48 for score averaging and 27.58 for joint prompting; this measures blending, not separate-object success.
astra.evidence_quote: In this paper, we cast the problem of combining multiple pre-trained diffusion models at the generation stage under a novel proposed framework termed superposition.

title: Steer Away From Mode Collisions: Improving Composition In Diffusion Models

claude.title: Steer Away From Mode Collisions: Improving Composition In Diffusion Models
claude.idea: Adds a corrector during sampling that steers away from regions where the joint prompt behaves like one of its single concepts, and keeps the guidance weights in a stable range.
claude.models: SDXL, with SD 1.5 among the baselines
claude.headline_result: Attend-and-Excite animal-animal prompts: BLIP-VQA 0.7441 and ImageReward 1.2342 for CO3, against 0.6980 and 0.8244 for Attend-and-Excite
claude.evidence_quote: Instead of re-training, we introduce a corrective sampling strategy that steers away from regions where the joint prompt behavior overlaps too strongly with any single concept in the prompt.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: Steer Away From Mode Collisions: Improving Composition In Diffusion Models
astra.idea: CO3 contrasts the joint-prompt prediction against individual-concept predictions using adaptive Tweedie-mean resampling and correction to reduce missing or colliding concepts.
astra.models: SDXL with DDIM; the same denoiser evaluates joint, individual and unconditional prompts. Setup: explicitly needs a joint prompt and its constituent concept prompts, although no additional training images are needed.
astra.datasets: Attend-and-Excite prompt categories; T2I-CompBench Complex; RareBench Concat, Relations and Complex.
astra.headline_result: Animal-Animal BLIP-VQA 0.7441 versus SDXL 0.6950; T2I-CompBench Complex ImageReward 0.4406 versus 0.3083.
astra.evidence_quote: This encourages the sampler to move away from the nearest mode, preventing collapse toward one dominant concept.

title: Rectify Then Diffuse: Disentangling Concepts Before Denoising Trajectory Unfolds

claude.title: Rectify Then Diffuse: Disentangling Concepts Before Denoising Trajectory Unfolds
claude.idea: Makes one bounded update to the starting latent that reduces overlap between the concepts' attention maps, then runs ordinary denoising.
claude.models: SDXL, with SD 1.5 among the baselines
claude.headline_result: AE-Bench object-object prompts: BLIP-VQA 0.7503 for RTD against 0.5146 for CO3, the 45.8% gain the abstract reports, while animal-object BLIP-VQA is lower at 0.8422 against 0.8878
claude.evidence_quote: To this end, we propose Rectify-then-Diffuse (RTD), a training-free framework that rectifies the initial allocation once before standard denoising.
claude.code_url: https://github.com/Z-yiwei/rectify-then-diffuse (the paper says code will be released)
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

title: MultiDiffusion: Fusing Diffusion Paths for Controlled Image Generation

claude.title: MultiDiffusion: Fusing Diffusion Paths for Controlled Image Generation
claude.idea: Runs one diffusion process per region or crop and reconciles them at every step through a shared optimization, using masks or boxes.
claude.models: Stable Diffusion
claude.headline_result: COCO region-based generation: IoU 0.26 +/- 0.12, against 0.17 for Blended Latent Diffusion and 0.16 for Stable Inpainting, with 0.43 for real COCO images
claude.evidence_quote: At the center of our approach is a new generation process, based on an optimization task that binds together multiple diffusion generation processes with a shared set of parameters or constraints.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: MultiDiffusion: Fusing Diffusion Paths for Controlled Image Generation
astra.idea: Solves a shared least-squares denoising problem over regions or crops so regional prompts and masks produce a coherent image.
astra.models: One pretrained Stable Diffusion v2 model reused across crops or regions. Setup: reported region benchmark uses a full-image caption for the background and regional prompts plus masks; the general regional formulation can use separate prompts.
astra.datasets: COCO validation subset for regional generation; text-to-panorama prompts.
astra.headline_result: COCO regional-generation IoU 0.26 ± 0.12 versus 0.18 ± 0.10 without bootstrapping.
astra.evidence_quote: In turn, the MultiDiffusion takes a global denoising sampling step reconciling all these different steps via least squares optimal solution.

title: TweedieMix: Improving Multi-Concept Fusion for Diffusion-based Image/Video Generation

astra.title: TweedieMix: Improving Multi-Concept Fusion for Diffusion-based Image/Video Generation
astra.idea: First encourages multiple objects with joint-prompt resampling, then mixes separately customized concepts in Tweedie-denoised space.
astra.models: Customized text-to-image diffusion models, primarily SDXL; image-to-video extensions including Stable Video Diffusion. Setup: requires a prompt containing multiple objects; concept customization is separate and shares a pretrained backbone.
astra.datasets: Custom Concept 101 combinations; personalized image and video examples.
astra.headline_result: Multi-concept CLIP image similarity 0.8311 and DINO image similarity 0.5950; the evaluation excludes images missing foreground objects.
astra.evidence_quote: During the initial steps, we apply a multiple object-aware sampling technique to ensure the inclusion of the desired target objects.

title: FreeFuse: Multi-Subject LoRA Fusion via Adaptive Token-Level Routing at Test Time

claude.title: FreeFuse: Multi-Subject LoRA Fusion via Adaptive Token-Level Routing at Test Time
claude.idea: Routes each separately trained subject LoRA to its own image region during inference, finding the regions from early flow-matching attention.
claude.models: FLUX.1-dev with subject LoRAs
claude.datasets: Multi-subject LoRA prompts scored on reference similarity, face identity and prompt following
claude.headline_result: ArcFace face similarity: 0.4275, against 0.3886 for LoRAShop
claude.evidence_quote: In contrast to prior studies that focus on retraining LoRAs to alleviate feature conflicts, our analysis shows that spatially routing LoRA residuals to their intended semantic regions provides an effective mechanism for suppressing direct cross-region LoRA interference while preserving the base model's global contextual reasoning.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: FreeFuse: Multi-Subject LoRA Fusion via Adaptive Token-Level Routing at Test Time
astra.idea: Routes separate subject LoRA residuals to automatically extracted subject regions while retaining the shared base model's global attention.
astra.models: FLUX flow-matching transformer with independently trained subject LoRAs; SDXL extension discussed. Setup: uses composite multi-subject prompts and a shared pretrained model, but needs no joint subject training images or user-drawn layout.
astra.datasets: Custom character-character and character-object prompt evaluations.
astra.headline_result: ArcFace identity similarity 0.4275 versus LoRAShop 0.3886 on the paper's multi-subject evaluation.
astra.evidence_quote: We propose a robust, training-free framework that mitigates feature conflicts among multiple LoRAs by spatially constraining their influence.

title: Local Mechanisms of Compositional Generalization in Conditional Diffusion

claude.title: Local Mechanisms of Compositional Generalization in Conditional Diffusion
claude.idea: Proves that conditional projective composition is equivalent to scores that depend sparsely on pixels and conditioners, and tests this on CLEVR and SDXL.
claude.models: Conditional diffusion models on CLEVR; SDXL
claude.headline_result: Training on 1-3 objects, the largest object count reached (Kmax) rises from 2 to 9 when local conditional scores are enforced on Experiment 2
claude.evidence_quote: In this paper, we prove an exact equivalence between a specific compositional structure ("conditional projective composition") (Bradley et al., 2025) and scores with sparse dependencies on both pixels and conditioners ("local conditional scores").
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: Local Mechanisms of Compositional Generalization in Conditional Diffusion
astra.idea: Connects conditional projective composition to local conditional scores and tests whether enforcing locality restores object-count generalization.
astra.models: Location- and color-conditioned CLEVR diffusion models; SDXL; Matryoshka Diffusion Model. Setup: explicitly tests object counts beyond training; the local intervention changes the architecture and requires training.
astra.datasets: CLEVR; semantic-category prompts for SDXL; Flickr-trained Matryoshka model analysis.
astra.headline_result: The local model trained on one object generalizes to five locations.
astra.where: Section 4, causal intervention; Figure 8 and Table 1.
astra.evidence_quote: Furthermore, we show that a causal intervention explicitly enforcing local conditional scores enables length generalization in a previously failing model.

title: Composing and Steering Diffusion Models with Generalized Feynman-Kac Correctors

claude.title: Composing and Steering Diffusion Models with Generalized Feynman-Kac Correctors
claude.idea: Extends Feynman-Kac correctors to sample from an arbitrary target function of several pretrained diffusion models, with optional reward steering.
claude.models: Diffusion models trained on subsets of MNIST digit classes; analytic Gaussian models
claude.headline_result: not stated
claude.evidence_quote: In this work, we introduce the generalized Feynman-Kac correctors (GFKC), a principled framework for sampling from an arbitrary target function of several pretrained diffusion models.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

title: Product of Experts for Visual Generation

claude.title: Product of Experts for Visual Generation
claude.idea: Samples from the product of several different experts, including generative models, a visual language model and simulators, using annealed importance sampling.
claude.models: FLUX.1 [dev], FLUX.1 Depth [dev], FLUX.1 Fill [dev], VQAScore, graphics engines and physics simulators
claude.datasets: 10 natural images with 3 object assets, Magic Insert characters, PhysGen3D scenes
claude.headline_result: Character insertion on the Magic Insert set: ImageReward 1.711 +/- 0.308, against 1.640 +/- 0.376 for SDEdit and 0.828 +/- 0.777 for FLUX-Fill
claude.evidence_quote: This training-free approach samples from the product distribution across experts via Annealed Importance Sampling (AIS).
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: Product of Experts for Visual Generation
astra.idea: Combines heterogeneous generative and discriminative experts with annealed MCMC and importance resampling, using conditional regional experts for more coherent visual composition.
astra.models: FLUX.1 Depth and Fill; Wan2.1 video models; autoregressive experts; VLM and physical-simulator constraints. Setup: reported tasks use a target scene specification, prompts, and reference or simulator inputs; no additional joint-model training is required.
astra.datasets: Graphics-rendered object insertion scenes; Magic Insert character insertion; physical-simulation video tasks.
astra.headline_result: Magic Insert scene evaluation ImageReward 1.711 ± 0.308 versus 1.169 ± 0.701 for Magic Insert.
astra.evidence_quote: We propose a probabilistic framework that combines information from these heterogeneous models, where expert models jointly shape a product distribution over outputs.

title: CoInD: Enabling Logical Compositions in Diffusion Models

claude.title: CoInD: Enabling Logical Compositions in Diffusion Models
claude.idea: Trains a conditional diffusion model with a penalty that enforces conditional independence between attribute marginals, so logical compositions hold on unseen attribute pairs.
claude.models: Conditional diffusion models; Stable Diffusion fine-tuning in an appendix
claude.headline_result: CelebA held-out smiling male, joint sampling: conformity score 8.63 and FID 43.97, against 2.51 and 61.21 for Composed GLIDE (the text says more than 4x, the table ratio is 3.4x)
claude.evidence_quote: It explicitly enforces statistical independence between the conditional marginal distributions by minimizing Fisher's divergence between the joint and marginal distributions.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: CoInD: Enabling Logical Compositions in Diffusion Models
astra.idea: Adds a training objective enforcing independence of conditional marginals so logical conjunction and negation work better on held-out attribute combinations.
astra.models: Conditional diffusion models with Fisher-divergence regularization; GLIDE comparison; Stable Diffusion fine-tuning extension. Setup: evaluates held-out target combinations, but requires training with attribute labels and an independence objective rather than merely combining frozen experts.
astra.datasets: Colored MNIST; Shapes3D; CelebA held-out smiling-male combination.
astra.headline_result: CelebA conjunction FID 43.76 for CoInD versus 95.41 for Composed GLIDE.
astra.evidence_quote: It explicitly enforces statistical independence between the conditional marginal distributions by minimizing Fisher’s divergence between the joint and marginal distributions.

title: Logical Guidance for the Exact Composition of Diffusion Models

claude.title: Logical Guidance for the Exact Composition of Diffusion Models
claude.idea: Gives a sufficient condition for computing exact guidance for Boolean formulas from atomic scores and posterior probabilities.
claude.models: Conditional diffusion models for images and protein structures
claude.datasets: CMNIST, Shapes3D, CelebA, protein structure tasks
claude.headline_result: CMNIST conformity score: 98.0% against 77.0% for constant guidance on mutually exclusive OR, and 80.4% for both on AND
claude.evidence_quote: Specifically, if a formula admits a circuit representation in which conjunctions combine conditionally independent subformulas and disjunctions combine subformulas that are either conditionally independent or mutually exclusive, exact logical guidance is achievable.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

title: Compositional Sculpting of Iterative Generative Processes

claude.title: Compositional Sculpting of Iterative Generative Processes
claude.idea: Defines harmonic-mean and contrast compositions of iterative generative models and samples them with classifier guidance.
claude.models: GFlowNets and diffusion models
claude.headline_result: not stated
claude.evidence_quote: We then introduce a method for sampling from these compositions built on classifier guidance.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: Compositional Sculpting of Iterative Generative Processes
astra.idea: Learns classifiers from component-model trajectories to guide harmonic-mean and contrast compositions, which reshape overlapping densities rather than establish separate-object extrapolation.
astra.models: Separately trained diffusion models with classifier guidance; GFlowNets. Setup: auxiliary classifiers are trained from component-generated samples; the demonstrated image components have overlapping support.
astra.datasets: Colored MNIST; MNIST subsets; molecular-generation and synthetic experiments.
astra.headline_result: not stated
astra.evidence_quote: We then introduce a method for sampling from these compositions built on classifier guidance.

title: Improving Compositional Generation with Diffusion Models Using Lift Scores

claude.title: Improving Compositional Generation with Diffusion Models Using Lift Scores
claude.idea: Scores each generated sample with a lift score for every single condition and rejects samples that fail the composed condition.
claude.models: Stable Diffusion 1.4, 2.1 and XL; separately trained 2D diffusion models
claude.datasets: 2D synthetic data, CLEVR positions, Attend-and-Excite benchmark
claude.headline_result: SDXL on Attend-and-Excite animal prompts: ImageReward 1.216 with CompLift at T=200, against 1.025 without it
claude.evidence_quote: By leveraging the lift scores, we evaluate whether generated samples align with each single condition and then compose the results to determine whether the composed prompt is satisfied.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

title: MCMC-Correction of Score-Based Diffusion Models for Model Composition

claude.title: MCMC-Correction of Score-Based Diffusion Models for Model Composition
claude.idea: Adds a Metropolis-Hastings-like acceptance rule based on line integrals of the score, so MCMC correction works on ordinary score models.
claude.models: Score-parameterized and energy-parameterized diffusion models
claude.headline_result: CIFAR-100 classifier-full guidance, 50k samples, score model: FID 13.3 with HMC-3C against 31.8 with reverse sampling
claude.evidence_quote: In this work, we address this limitation by retaining score parameterization and introducing a novel MH-like acceptance rule based on line integration of the score function.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

title: Classifier-Free Guidance is a Predictor-Corrector

astra.title: Classifier-Free Guidance is a Predictor-Corrector
astra.idea: Shows that guided DDPM and DDIM need not sample the intended powered density and interprets stochastic CFG as a denoising predictor plus a Langevin sharpening corrector.
astra.models: DDPM and DDIM guidance; analytic Gaussian examples; SDXL predictor-corrector demonstration. Setup: theoretical analysis of conditional and unconditional scores; no joint-concept dataset is required.
astra.datasets: Synthetic Gaussian and Gaussian-mixture counterexamples; qualitative SDXL prompts.
astra.headline_result: not stated
astra.evidence_quote: PCG alternates between denoising steps and Langevin dynamics steps.

title: Composition and Control with Distilled Energy Diffusion Models and Sequential Monte Carlo

claude.title: Composition and Control with Distilled Energy Diffusion Models and Sequential Monte Carlo
claude.idea: Distills pretrained diffusion models into energy functions and uses their potentials in sequential Monte Carlo to compose separately trained models.
claude.models: Energy-parameterized diffusion models distilled from EDM teachers
claude.headline_result: not stated for composition: the CelebA male AND glasses result in Section 5.3 and Figure 7 is qualitative
claude.evidence_quote: The Feynman Kac model formalism enables composition and low temperature sampling through sequential Monte Carlo.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

title: Training-free Conditional Object Composition for Multi-object Image Generation with Diffusion Models

astra.title: Training-free Conditional Object Composition for Multi-object Image Generation with Diffusion Models
astra.idea: Generates a subset of requested objects first, then inserts the remaining object with inpainting and layout guidance, selecting the decomposition using attention or a detector.
astra.models: SDXL; attention-based selection or Faster R-CNN selection; YOLOv11-L evaluation. Setup: uses a multi-object prompt, and evaluation object sets are taken from real COCO images in which the objects co-occur.
astra.datasets: MS COCO object co-occurrence prompt sets.
astra.headline_result: For six objects, success rate is 35.8 ± 5.3% with detector selection and 25.2 ± 4.7% with attention selection, versus SDXL 19.2 ± 3.3%.
astra.evidence_quote: To enable effective composition, we adopt an inpainting-based formulation with layout guidance to preserve existing regions and encourage spatially coherent placement.

title: Attend-and-Excite: Attention-Based Semantic Guidance for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

claude.title: Attend-and-Excite: Attention-Based Semantic Guidance for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
claude.idea: Updates the latent during sampling so the cross-attention map of every subject token reaches a strong activation.
claude.models: Stable Diffusion
claude.datasets: Animal-animal, animal-object and object-object prompt sets
claude.headline_result: User study with 65 respondents on animal-animal prompts: Attend-and-Excite chosen 90.70% of the time, against 2.32% for Stable Diffusion and 0% for Composable Diffusion
claude.evidence_quote: Using an attention-based formulation of GSN, dubbed Attend-and-Excite, we guide the model to refine the cross-attention units to attend to all subject tokens in the text prompt and strengthen - or excite - their activations, encouraging the model to generate all subjects described in the text prompt.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: Attend-and-Excite: Attention-Based Semantic Guidance for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
astra.idea: Updates the noisy latent to strengthen the most neglected subject's cross-attention, encouraging all prompted objects to appear.
astra.models: Stable Diffusion with inference-time cross-attention optimization. Setup: requires a joint text prompt and its subject tokens; no extra training images are needed.
astra.datasets: Animal-Animal, Animal-Object and Object-Object prompt benchmark; complex multi-subject prompts.
astra.headline_result: Animal-Animal CLIP text-text similarity between prompt and BLIP caption is 0.806 versus 0.767 for Stable Diffusion.
astra.evidence_quote: As such, we define a loss objective that attempts to maximize the attention values for each subject token.

title: Test-Time Compositional Generalization in Diffusion Models via Concept Discovery

claude.title: Test-Time Compositional Generalization in Diffusion Models via Concept Discovery
claude.idea: Recovers density modes from one out-of-distribution query image, combines them into an analytic product-of-experts teacher, and can train a low-rank adapter on its samples.
claude.models: Pretrained conditional diffusion model with a new class embedding and low-rank adapter
claude.datasets: ColorMNIST (40 held-out compositions), CelebA (23 held-out compositions)
claude.headline_result: ColorMNIST faithfulness F1: 75.3% +/- 3.1 for the product of experts and 87.6% +/- 2.1 with the adapter, against 0.0% for the query-only baseline
claude.evidence_quote: These results suggest that the time-indexed score geometry of the diffusion model contains reusable density-mode concepts that support test-time compositional generation without a predefined concept library.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: Test-Time Compositional Generalization in Diffusion Models via Concept Discovery
astra.idea: Discovers density-mode prototypes from a pretrained score field and combines them into a Gaussian product teacher, optionally distilled into a LoRA, to reproduce an unseen composition specified by an example.
astra.models: Pretrained conditional UNet; analytic Gaussian product-of-experts teacher; learned class embedding and LoRA. Setup: requires a single out-of-distribution query image showing the desired composition.
astra.datasets: ColorMNIST and CelebA with held-out attribute combinations.
astra.headline_result: CelebA generalization FID 140.3 for the analytic PoE; LoRA generalization F1 24.7% versus query-only 20.2%.
astra.evidence_quote: On held-out composition benchmarks built from ColorMNIST and CelebA, both the analytic PoE sampler and the low-rank adapted model outperform query-only and nearest trained-class baselines.

title: Token Merging for Training-Free Semantic Binding in Text-to-Image Synthesis

claude.title: Token Merging for Training-Free Semantic Binding in Text-to-Image Synthesis
claude.idea: Merges an object's related tokens into one composite token so they share a cross-attention map, then refines it with entropy and binding losses.
claude.models: SDXL
claude.datasets: T2I-CompBench, a GPT-4o object binding benchmark
claude.headline_result: T2I-CompBench color binding, BLIP-VQA: 0.7656 for ToMe on SDXL against 0.6369 for SDXL
claude.evidence_quote: We introduce a novel method called Token Merging (ToMe), which enhances semantic binding by aggregating relevant tokens into a single composite token.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: Token Merging for Training-Free Semantic Binding in Text-to-Image Synthesis
astra.idea: Merges each object's related tokens into a composite token and refines token embeddings to improve attribute and sub-object binding.
astra.models: SDXL; SpaCy parsing; composite-token optimization and end-token substitution. Setup: syntactically parses a joint prompt; no additional model training is required.
astra.datasets: T2I-CompBench attribute-binding subsets; proposed GPT-4o object-binding benchmark.
astra.headline_result: GPT-4o object-binding score 0.9549 versus SDXL 0.4907.
astra.evidence_quote: We introduce a novel method called Token Merging (ToMe), which enhances semantic binding by aggregating relevant tokens into a single composite token.

title: PiCo: Enhancing Text-Image Alignment with Improved Noise Selection and Precise Mask Control in Diffusion Models

claude.title: PiCo: Enhancing Text-Image Alignment with Improved Noise Selection and Precise Mask Control in Diffusion Models
claude.idea: Picks a suitable starting noise with a fast check and uses generated pixel masks to modulate cross-attention.
claude.models: Stable Diffusion v2.1
claude.datasets: CC-500, T2I-CompBench, COCO reference set for FID
claude.headline_result: Human evaluation of attribute binding, Both column with selected noise: 41.8 for PiCo, against 38.0 for Attend-and-Excite and 34.7 for Stable Diffusion
claude.evidence_quote: We then propose PiCo (Pick-and-Control), a novel training-free approach with two key components to tackle these two factors.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: PiCo: Enhancing Text-Image Alignment with Improved Noise Selection and Precise Mask Control in Diffusion Models
astra.idea: Selects promising initial noise and uses referring masks to control cross-attention so objects and attributes are less often omitted or mixed.
astra.models: Stable Diffusion with noise selection and referring-mask control. Setup: evaluates and controls generation against a joint prompt; no model fine-tuning is required.
astra.datasets: CC-500; T2I-CompBench attribute and complex-composition prompts; MS COCO for image-quality metrics.
astra.headline_result: VQAScore 0.50 on T2I-CompBench prompts with selected noise, versus 0.45 for Stable Diffusion under the same noise-selection setting.
astra.where: Table I (objective metrics, selected noise); evaluation protocol in the experiments section.
astra.evidence_quote: Second, we introduce a referring mask module to generate pixel-level masks and to precisely modulate the cross-attention maps.

title: Diffusion Domain Expansion: Learning to Coordinate Pre-trained Diffusion Models

claude.title: Diffusion Domain Expansion: Learning to Coordinate Pre-trained Diffusion Models
claude.venue: ICML 2024 Workshop on Structured Probabilistic Inference and Generative Modeling
claude.idea: Trains a small coordinator network on the denoised outputs of a frozen pretrained model so it can generate larger objects or handle more conditions.
claude.models: Pretrained UNet diffusion models with a ViT coordinator
claude.headline_result: CLEVR with 5 conditions using the Heun sampler: accuracy 44.5% for DDE, against 36.3% for MultiDiffusion and 33.6% for Reduce Reuse Recycle
claude.evidence_quote: Our method employs a compact trainable network designed to coordinate the denoised outputs of pre-trained diffusion models.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: Diffusion Domain Expansion: Learning to Coordinate Pre-trained Diffusion Models
astra.venue: ICML 2024 SPIGM Workshop (as stated in arXiv comments; arXiv submission is 2026)
astra.idea: Trains a coordinator over pretrained denoiser outputs to generalize to larger domains or more conditioning inputs than the coordinator saw during training.
astra.models: Pretrained UNet diffusion models with a ViT coordinator. Setup: coordinator training uses larger objects or multiple conditioning inputs, so it does not meet the no-joint-data requirement.
astra.datasets: Slakh2100; CLEVR; Google Maps satellite-image dataset.
astra.headline_result: CLEVR accuracy with five conditioning locations is 44.5 for DDE with Heun versus 33.6 for RRR with Heun.
astra.evidence_quote: Our method employs a compact trainable network designed to coordinate the denoised outputs of pre-trained diffusion models.

title: GenEval: An Object-Focused Framework for Evaluating Text-to-Image Alignment

claude.title: GenEval: An Object-Focused Framework for Evaluating Text-to-Image Alignment
claude.idea: Scores generated images with an object detector and color classifier on tasks that include two-object co-occurrence.
claude.models: Stable Diffusion v2.1, SDXL, IF-XL and other open text-to-image models
claude.headline_result: 83% agreement with human annotators, against 88% agreement between annotators, on 6,000 annotations over 1,200 images
claude.evidence_quote: In this paper, we introduce GenEval, an object-focused framework to evaluate compositional image properties such as object co-occurrence, position, count, and color.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: GenEval: An Object-Focused Framework for Evaluating Text-to-Image Alignment
astra.idea: Uses object detection, segmentation and color classification to check object presence, count, position and attribute binding separately.
astra.models: Mask2Former and CLIP evaluator; Stable Diffusion variants, SDXL, DeepFloyd IF and minDALL-E. Setup: evaluation uses compositional target prompts, but does not supply joint training data to the generator.
astra.datasets: GenEval templated prompts based on COCO object categories; human-agreement study.
astra.headline_result: GenEval agrees with human annotators on 83% of images, compared with 88% interannotator agreement.
astra.evidence_quote: In this paper, we introduce GenEval, an object-focused framework to evaluate compositional image properties such as object co-occurrence, position, count, and color.

title: T2I-CompBench++: An Enhanced and Comprehensive Benchmark for Compositional Text-to-image Generation

claude.title: T2I-CompBench++: An Enhanced and Comprehensive Benchmark for Compositional Text-to-image Generation
claude.venue: NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks (conference version); arXiv now holds a journal version
claude.idea: Provides a prompt benchmark and metrics for attribute binding, object relationships, numeracy and complex compositions.
claude.models: 11 text-to-image models including FLUX.1, SD3, DALLE-3, PixArt-alpha and SD-XL
claude.headline_result: 8,000 compositional prompts in four groups, used to benchmark 11 models
claude.evidence_quote: T2I-CompBench++ comprises 8,000 compositional text prompts categorized into four primary groups: attribute binding, object relationships, generative numeracy, and complex compositions.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: T2I-CompBench++: An Enhanced and Comprehensive Benchmark for Compositional Text-to-image Generation
astra.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, 2025
astra.idea: Extends T2I-CompBench to test attribute binding, relationships, numeracy and complex scenes with category-specific VQA and detection metrics.
astra.models: BLIP-VQA, UniDet, CLIP and multimodal evaluators; Stable Diffusion variants, FLUX.1, DALL-E 3, PixArt and compositional baselines. Setup: evaluation requires compositional prompts; its GORS baseline fine-tunes on reward-selected generated image-prompt pairs.
astra.datasets: T2I-CompBench and expanded T2I-CompBench++; the selected title is the arXiv journal revision rather than the original conference title.
astra.headline_result: On color binding, BLIP-VQA has human-ranking Spearman rho 0.7958 versus CLIP 0.2773.
astra.evidence_quote: In addition to the benchmark, we propose enhanced evaluation metrics designed to assess these diverse compositional challenges.

title: ISAC: Training-Free Instance-to-Semantic Attention Control for Multi-Instance Generation

claude.title: ISAC: Training-Free Instance-to-Semantic Attention Control for Multi-Instance Generation
claude.idea: Stabilizes instance layouts in self-attention during early denoising, then binds cross-attention semantics inside those instances without fine-tuning.
claude.models: SD 1.5, SD 3.5-M and other diffusion backbones
claude.headline_result: IntraCompBench multi-class subset, 2-item column: 98% for SD 3.5-M with ISAC against 62% for SD 3.5-M alone
claude.evidence_quote: By contrast, self-attention exposes class-agnostic instance layouts during early denoising.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

title: GenEval 2: Addressing Benchmark Drift in Text-to-Image Evaluation

claude.title: GenEval 2: Addressing Benchmark Drift in Text-to-Image Evaluation
claude.idea: Shows that GenEval's automatic judge has drifted from human judgment and introduces a harder benchmark with the Soft-TIFA scoring method.
claude.models: 8 text-to-image models in the human study, including Gemini 2.5 Flash Image; Qwen3-VL as the VQA judge
claude.headline_result: GenEval's reported score differs from human judgment by up to 17.7% on current models, and Gemini 2.5 Flash Image scores 96.7% under human evaluation
claude.evidence_quote: To help fill this benchmarking gap, we introduce a new benchmark, GenEval 2, with improved coverage of primitive visual concepts and higher degrees of compositionality, which we show is more challenging for current models.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

astra.title: GenEval 2: Addressing Benchmark Drift in Text-to-Image Evaluation
astra.idea: Audits drift in GenEval and introduces more compositional prompts with Soft-TIFA scoring of individual visual requirements.
astra.models: Soft-TIFA with an open-source VQA model; Stable Diffusion variants, FLUX.1-dev, Bagel, Qwen-Image and Gemini image generation. Setup: evaluation specifies multi-object targets through prompts; no generator training on these targets is required.
astra.datasets: GenEval audit; GenEval 2; human annotations of prompt and atom correctness.
astra.headline_result: GenEval underestimates Gemini 2.5 Flash Image's human score by 17.7 percentage points.
astra.evidence_quote: We also introduce Soft-TIFA, an evaluation method tailored to GenEval 2’s templated and compositional structure.

title: BoxDiff: Text-to-Image Synthesis with Training-Free Box-Constrained Diffusion

astra.title: BoxDiff: Text-to-Image Synthesis with Training-Free Box-Constrained Diffusion
astra.idea: Constrains token attention inside, outside and along the boundaries of boxes to place distinct objects without retraining.
astra.models: Stable Diffusion; plug-in evaluation with GLIGEN. Setup: uses a joint text prompt and user-specified boxes or scribbles, but no new paired training data.
astra.datasets: New collected image/layout set excluding overlap with COCO and Visual Genome.
astra.headline_result: Stable Diffusion plus BoxDiff achieves YOLO AP 22.3 versus 2.8 without BoxDiff.
astra.evidence_quote: Beyond that, BoxDiff can interact with other types of conditions such as scribble.

title: Be Decisive: Noise-Induced Layouts for Multi-Subject Generation

claude.title: Be Decisive: Noise-Induced Layouts for Multi-Subject Generation
claude.idea: Predicts a soft subject layout from the initial noise with a small network and refines it through denoising to keep subjects separate.
claude.models: SDXL
claude.headline_result: T2I-CompBench multi-class: 0.723 for this method, against 0.676 for SDXL and 0.898 for LMD+, which needs training
claude.evidence_quote: In this work, we introduce a new approach that predicts a spatial layout aligned with the prompt, derived from the initial noise, and refines it throughout the denoising process.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

title: Be Yourself: Bounded Attention for Multi-Subject Text-to-Image Generation

claude.title: Be Yourself: Bounded Attention for Multi-Subject Text-to-Image Generation
claude.idea: Bounds attention between subjects during sampling so that their features do not leak into one another, using a given layout.
claude.models: Stable Diffusion, SDXL
claude.headline_result: DrawBench: F1 0.82 and accuracy 0.36, against 0.73 and 0.19 for Stable Diffusion
claude.evidence_quote: Bounded Attention prevents detrimental leakage among subjects and enables guiding the generation to promote each subject's individuality, even with complex multi-subject conditioning.
claude.read: abstract, results tables and targeted passages

title: GLIGEN: Open-Set Grounded Text-to-Image Generation

astra.title: GLIGEN: Open-Set Grounded Text-to-Image Generation
astra.idea: Adds trainable gated attention layers to a frozen text-to-image model so entity descriptions and spatial inputs control object placement.
astra.models: Frozen latent diffusion and Stable Diffusion backbones with new grounding layers. Setup: trains added layers on grounded image annotations and uses a scene-level set of entities and locations; target combinations can be novel.
astra.datasets: COCO; LVIS; grounded text-to-image and inpainting experiments.
astra.headline_result: COCO2014 detection-conditioned GLIGEN obtains FID 5.61 and YOLO AP 24.0.
astra.evidence_quote: With the above aims, we propose a method for providing new grounding conditional inputs to pretrained text-to-image diffusion models.

title: Training-Free Structured Diffusion Guidance for Compositional Text-to-Image Synthesis

astra.title: Training-Free Structured Diffusion Guidance for Compositional Text-to-Image Synthesis
astra.idea: Uses linguistic structure to construct cross-attention features for separate noun phrases, improving attribute binding and concept conjunction.
astra.models: Stable Diffusion with structured cross-attention. Setup: parses a joint prompt into constituent phrases; no extra training samples are needed.
astra.datasets: ABC-6K; CC-500; MS COCO captions.
astra.headline_result: On ABC-6K, human text-image alignment preference is 42.2% wins versus 35.6% losses against Stable Diffusion, after filtering the most similar pairs.
astra.evidence_quote: Therefore, by manipulating the cross-attention representations based on linguistic insights, we can better preserve the compositional semantics in the generated image.

title: Linguistic Binding in Diffusion Models: Enhancing Attribute Correspondence through Attention Map Alignment

astra.title: Linguistic Binding in Diffusion Models: Enhancing Attribute Correspondence through Attention Map Alignment
astra.idea: SynGen parses entity-modifier relationships and optimizes cross-attention to bind related tokens while separating unrelated concepts.
astra.models: Stable Diffusion with inference-time attention loss; comparisons with Attend-and-Excite and Structured Diffusion. Setup: requires a joint prompt whose syntax supplies bindings; no model retraining is needed.
astra.datasets: ABC-6K; Attend-and-Excite attribute prompts; DVMP challenge set.
astra.headline_result: On ABC-6K, SynGen receives 28.00% of majority votes for concept separation versus 11.17% for Attend-and-Excite.
astra.evidence_quote: Specifically, we encourage large overlap between attention maps of entities and their modifiers, and small overlap with other entities and modifier words.

title: From Global to Factor-Wise Expert Composition in Discrete Diffusion Models

astra.title: From Global to Factor-Wise Expert Composition in Discrete Diffusion Models
astra.idea: FactorDiff routes each discrete grid position to the most confident expert instead of assigning one mixture weight per sample, offering a regional composition comparison outside natural-image diffusion.
astra.models: Masked discrete diffusion experts for occupancy, foreground color and full-grid prediction; convolutional and transformer iterative-refinement backbones. Setup: demonstrates experts trained on different objectives from a common grid-task corpus, not disjoint concept-image datasets.
astra.datasets: ARC-AGI-1 task subset with RE-ARC-generated held-out IID examples.
astra.headline_result: Color-plus-occupancy routing reaches 90.5% exact-grid accuracy versus 78.4% for FKC; this is the selected-task IID evaluation, not the full ARC test benchmark.
astra.evidence_quote: We exploit this factorization to compose experts at the variable level.

title: When Do Diffusion Models learn to Generate Multiple Objects?

astra.title: When Do Diffusion Models learn to Generate Multiple Objects?
astra.idea: Uses the controlled mosaic generator to isolate scene complexity, concept imbalance and held-out combinations as causes of multi-object generation failure.
astra.models: Latent U-Net diffusion and DiT flow-matching models with a frozen Stable Diffusion VAE. Setup: the compositional-generalization experiments explicitly withhold target factor pairs, alongside experiments on observed concepts.
astra.datasets: mosaic synthetic attribution, spatial-relation and counting tasks.
astra.headline_result: Attribution and spatial relations exceed 90% accuracy in the base concept-generalization setting, including highly skewed data, while counting has a low-data failure regime.
astra.evidence_quote: Moreover, compositional generalization collapses as more concept combinations are held out during training.
